creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`kan commit` writes `chore: update kan files` when no `-m` is given (`internal/cli/commit.go:68`). Fine in the abstract, wrong in most repos: it lands in the history of a project that has its own commit convention and does not follow it.

In muster the convention for board changes is `docs(kan): <what changed>`, so `kan commit` there is always either `-m "..."` or a `kan commit` followed by `git commit --amend` - twice in one session, both times an amend, because the default is what you get when you forget.

`-m` already covers the one-off. What is missing is a per-project default, so the correct subject is the one you get by typing nothing.

`.kan/config.toml` looks like the natural home - already per-project, already carrying project-level settings:

```toml
kan_schema = "project/2"
id = "p_BDnFKuao"
name = "kan"

commit_message = "docs(kan): update the board"
```

Worth deciding: fixed string, or a template with something substitutable in it (the cards touched, the columns they moved between). A fixed string is most of the value and none of the design work; a template is the thing somebody asks for next.

The current default is quoted in `extras/skill/SKILL.md` and `web/src/docs/cli.md`, plus the generated copies under `internal/api/dist/`, so whatever the wording becomes has to reach those too.
title: let a project set the default kan commit message
